subject.title: backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)

question: What restore-safe core behavior should `openclaw backup create` support for large state directories: native smart/custom exclusions, a minimal completion/error fix, or a documented decision that current coarse scopes are the intended core boundary?
rationale: Choosing default exclusions and protected backup contents affects restore completeness and security, and the linked PR is already under review with unresolved proof and merge-risk concerns.

options.title: Narrow And Review Native Exclusions
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after resolving conflicts, real proof, protected-path semantics, and external-asset behavior.

options.title: Ship Minimal Reliability First
options.body: Fix the archive path to complete or fail clearly with progress or size guidance, while deferring smart/custom exclusions to a separate native exclude-pattern decision.

options.title: Defer Core Scope Expansion
options.body: Document current core backup limits and point users to plugin or workaround options only if maintainers explicitly decide native exclusions are outside core for now.

recommendation.title: Narrow And Review Native Exclusions
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after resolving conflicts, real proof, protected-path semantics, and external-asset behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current routing signal for product policy while original and recent backup contributors provide implementation context.
